_comment: Live config. Both Gemini Pro-tier options are dead ends: gemini-3.1-pro-preview hit a hard 429 quota-exceeded (needs billing enabled, not just a low free allowance) and gemini-2.5-pro came back 404 'no longer available to new users' - a real decommission, not a rate issue. A role's value can be a single {provider, model, ...} dict, or a LIST of them - a fallback chain tried in preference order, falling back only once a candidate's own internal retries are fully exhausted (see providers.call_model/_dispatch). Groq stays on skeleton/summariser ONLY - a large canon.md + motif-ledger payload hit a 413 'tokens per minute (TPM): Limit 8000' on Groq even on its biggest model, so it's kept only where the payload is provably small (skeleton never includes the motif section; summariser never sends canon.md at all); both have run there without a single TPM failure across the whole project. 2026-09-23: Mistral and Cerebras REMOVED entirely, from every role - both confirmed genuinely non-functional on this account, not just unlucky timing. Mistral: 429 rate_limited on every single attempt it was ever reached across four separate incidents spanning weeks (two before the fallback-chain redesign, two after) - including isolated single calls, minutes apart, that still failed for the model's whole ~10.5-minute retry budget. Mistral's own published free-tier throughput (1-5 req/s) can't explain that on a pipeline that only ever sends one request at a time; this looks like an inactive/zero free quota on this key, not a rate limit being hit. Cerebras: even after fixing its dead llama3.3-70b model ID (see prior history below) to gpt-oss-120b, the very next time it was reached (editor, after Gemini genuinely demand-spiked and Mistral 429'd) it came back a flat 402 'Payment required to access this resource... quota' - this account's Cerebras free trial credit is spent and nothing further will succeed without adding billing, a real money decision, not something to route around in code. Both were last-resort candidates on action/character/atmosphere/unify/editor; those roles now chain within Gemini only (flash-lite -> flash-3.6, or the reverse for editor). editor in particular now has NO fallback at all (a single gemini-3.6-flash dict) - it can't use flash-lite as a second candidate without risking grading unify's own output when both land on a fallback at once, and no other provider currently works. That's a real, known gap, not an oversight: if Gemini has a bad night hard enough that editor's own retries run out, the run will crash and discard cleanly (existing behavior), and the next scheduled run picks it back up - acceptable under this project's 'a day late beats shipping something broken' priority, but worth reopening if Gemini's editor pass starts failing outright instead of just retrying. Earlier history, still true: (1) 2026-09-20, swapped action/character/atmosphere/unify off gemini-3.6-flash onto gemini-3.5-flash-lite, moved editor the other way (3.5-flash-lite -> 3.6-flash), after three straight days of 503 'high demand' storms outlasting the full retry backoff - the run that nailed it down failed on action, the very FIRST call of a fresh regeneration, proving it's the model under sustained load, not any one pass's payload. (2) Every role turned into an explicit fallback chain, at the user's direct request to hedge against a whole provider having a bad night - Mistral/Cerebras were that hedge; both turned out not to work, hence their removal above. (3) run_chapter.py caps how many fresh prose passes ONE run attempts (MAX_NEW_PASSES_PER_RUN, default 2) before stopping cleanly (exit 0) and leaving the rest for the next scheduled fire. (4) Groq removed from the five heavy roles after a live 413 TPM failure on a big payload (see above). summariser also carries reasoning_effort/reasoning_format on its Groq candidate - its original model (qwen/qwen3.6-27b) was a reasoning model that emitted <think>...</think> as literal text sharing the same token budget as the real answer, burning through its budget without ever finishing its reasoning, let alone writing the summary. These fields (read by providers._openai_compatible, ignored by candidates that don't set them) disable reasoning outright and strip it from the response as a second line of defense. qwen/qwen3.6-27b itself was then decommissioned outright (404 model_not_found) - moved summariser's primary to openai/gpt-oss-20b, the smaller sibling of skeleton's gpt-oss-120b: same family, distinct model ID so no shared TPM concerns, small enough for a task that never sends canon.md anyway. Two live 400s fixing that: qwen accepted reasoning_effort 'none' but gpt-oss only accepts low/medium/high (set to 'low'), and reasoning_format isn't supported by gpt-oss at all - had to drop it. Not a problem in practice: gpt-oss puts reasoning in its own response field rather than qwen's literal inline tags, so the content field _openai_compatible() reads was never going to carry reasoning text regardless. _strip_thinking() in passes.py stays as a no-cost safety net for whatever model ends up on this role next. IMPORTANT: never push a new commit to main while a draft.yml run is in progress - its own end-of-run checkpoint commit/push can get rejected as a non-fast-forward conflict, silently losing that run's work (caught live doing exactly this).
